   - Provide pre-filled SOC2 evidence packet and pointer doc (we can surface templates). Owner: Kimberly.
   - Offer a temporary dedicated pool start (reserve GPU capacity to meet KPIs). Owner: Marcus (need estimate).
3) Commercial/terms: hold price but reserve right to approve small credit if procurement delay exceeds X (ask Rishi to advise).

- Marcus: GPU provisioning estimate + earliest start date (ETA 2028-04-13) — attachment: proposed-map-v2.xlsx
- Monica: Identify 3 acceptance scenarios and condense POC plan (ETA 2028-04-14)
- Rishi: Flag commercial risk and escalation ladder for procurement asks (ETA 2028-04-14)
- Kimberly: Draft an updated MAP PDF and send to Sarah with conservative target (ETA 2028-05-04)

Quick commercial read — procurement patterns for deals like ACME-7890:

- If evaluation extends beyond the original planned close, procurement tends to request a credit (typical ask 10–25%). They've flagged "contingency credit" language as their negotiation lever.
- Approving any credit requires VP/Finance sign-off for account >$250k (we should confirm band).

Escalation ladder suggestion (short):
1) AE (Kim) tries to preserve list price and offers non-monetary concessions (extended onboarding hours, extra training days).
2) If procurement pushes credit >10%, escalate to me for a one-time approval up to 10% (I will confirm with finance).
3) >10% requires Sales Leader + Finance approval and must include a firm close-date re-commitment and MAP checksum.

Given Marcus's note on provisional pre-provisioning, we can offer conditional hold without discount while procurement completes review — but if they insist on a credit we should ask for written confirmation of the procurement timeline and commit to the conservative close (2028-06-18) before offering credits.

Rishi
Sr. Sales Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
